target_claim: In the verification that the constructed rank candidate satisfies axiom (R2), the proof asserts for ARBITRARY X = {x_1,...,x_q} ⊆ S and ARBITRARY y ∈ S (no assumption y ∉ X) that rho(X ∪ {y}) − rho(X) = t(x_1,...,x_q,y) − t(x_1,...,x_q), and hence equals theta(x_1,...,x_q,y)_{q+1}, which is 1 whenever no C ∈ 𝒞 satisfies y ∈ C ⊆ {x_1,...,x_q,y}. The case y ∈ X is never excluded, and in that case the asserted equality (and the derived value) is false: it yields rho(X ∪ {y}) = rho(X) + 1 for X ∪ {y} = X. (Note the author does exclude this case in Lemma 2, stating "Let X ⊆ S and y ∈ S \ X", showing the omission in the (R2) argument is a real case gap, not a notational convention.)
